strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing practical inefficiency in current LLM-based repair systems
Consistent empirical improvements across three different base models (GPT-4o, GPT-5, DeepSeek-V3) demonstrating generalizability
Significant computational efficiency gains over forward search baseline (9.71× fewer LLM calls, 2.47× fewer tokens) with superior performance
Comprehensive ablation studies validating each component (Exemplar Guardian: -4-5.6%, MCTS comparison, exemplar similarity sensitivity)
Proper statistical methodology including McNemar's test, stability analysis (90% Agree@3), and difficulty-stratified evaluation
Clear presentation of three-stage pipeline with good integration into existing repair frameworks
Practical applicability to standard autoregressive LLMs without fine-tuning
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: outcome-conditioned generation via prompting is not fundamentally new; framing as 'backward reasoning distillation' overstates the contribution relative to standard in-context conditioning
Narrow evaluation scope restricts generalizability: only SWE-Bench Lite (300 issues), predominantly Python, 13 repositories—no evaluation on Java, C++, JavaScript or other languages
Reproducibility concerns: evaluation uses future-dated LLM versions unavailable at review time (gpt-5-2025-08-07); exact prompts for all stages not fully specified; no code repository provided

Incomplete analysis of Exemplar Guardian: low stability on 'Misleading' category (77.8% vs 91.4% for others); no evidence that transferability scores correlate with actual performance gains; no per-issue breakdown of Guardian failures
Limited exemplar coverage unexplored: only 65% of test issues receive exemplars (195/300 for GPT-4o)—what about remaining 35%? No analysis of repository characteristics enabling effective transfer

Modest empirical improvements: 10.4% over Agentless baseline is incremental; still trails SWE-Search by 6.7% on same model; marginal improvements in function-level localization on some models suggest gains may be patch-generation focused

Missing analyses: no qualitative examples of exemplar selection/rejection decisions, no case studies of successful transfers, no error analysis of failure modes, insufficient investigation of when negative transfer occurs
Weak baseline comparisons: custom-built MCTS baseline is not from published system; limited comparison with other retrieval-based repair methods (RelRepair, ExpeRepair) cited in related work
Practical limitations underexplored: method requires suitable repository history—new/sparse projects cannot benefit; three-file modification constraint may exclude important complex repairs
Technical claims lack empirical validation: assertion that conditioning 'narrows plausible continuations' (p.5) is stated without analysis of text diversity or probability distributions

strengths: Novel approach to backward reasoning distillation from verified outcomes, well-motivated as alternative to forward search
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three LLM backbones (GPT-4o, GPT-5, DeepSeek-V3) with proper statistical testing (McNemar's test, p<0.001)
Consistent improvements over strong baselines with good ablation studies demonstrating each component's necessity
Significant practical efficiency gains: 9.71× fewer LLM calls and 2.47× fewer tokens than MCTS, enabling scalable inference-time improvement
Excellent reproducibility support with full prompts in appendices and implementation details clearly specified
Generalization validation on two different scaffolds (Agentless and mini-SWE-agent) showing improvements aren't scaffold-specific
Stability analysis of Exemplar Guardian showing 90% label agreement across runs, building confidence in the filtering mechanism
weaknesses: Moderate magnitude of improvements (10.4% on Pass@1: 27.3%→37.7% with GPT-4o); absolute success rate remains modest (~38%); limited analysis of which bug types benefit most or failure modes
Significant practical limitation to same-repository bugs severely restricts applicability; new or sparsely-maintained repositories cannot benefit; impact quantification lacking
Key design choices lack principled justification: why ≤3 files for patches, why top-5 initial candidates, why five specific dimensions for Exemplar Guardian; no ablations provided

Incomplete analysis of reasoning distillation quality: no concrete examples of distilled plans, no independent evaluation of plan quality beyond final patches, why 'Exemplar & Patch (no plan)' fails badly unexplained
Limited generalization testing: only 2 scaffolds evaluated (Agentless and mini-SWE-agent), no open-source LLM results, evaluation restricted to Python projects in SWE-Bench Lite
Dependence on LLM-based Exemplar Guardian filtering without comparing to simpler heuristics; no analysis of false positives/negatives or how wrong exemplars affect outcomes
Filtering dataset to ≤3 file modifications may systematically bias toward simpler bugs and exclude harder repairs; no analysis of excluded data

Backward distillation constructs 'retrospectively valid' plans rather than recovering actual reasoning; unclear whether plans capture genuine debugging patterns or merely post-hoc rationalizations; similarity to human reasoning unexplored

Circular evaluation effect: ConRAD falls back to Agentless baseline when Exemplar Guardian rejects exemplars (195/300 accepted in Table 3), preventing worse-than-baseline outcomes; selection bias not clearly discussed
